content: User prefers tech-lead reviews to avoid bookkeeping-only "close tracking" actions. Resolved items should be recorded in summary (e.g., resolved-by-decomposition) and excluded from Priority Actions/Persistent Issues.
User wants items they mention to be added one-by-one into knowledge as backlog entries from now on.
Implement thread fork feature.
Implement skill runtime reload feature.

User-facing custom agent management is still incomplete: runtime can discover and spawn file-based custom agents from .diligent/agents/*/AGENT.md, but Web/CLI/protocol do not yet provide create/upload/manage flows comparable to skills.
Support using tool plugins directly in TypeScript form without build/package step; reference pi-mono approach for detailed design.
Introduce domain-dedicated tech-lead reviewers (core, runtime, web, tui) instead of only whole-repo review, and run them on GitHub Runner for automated checks.
On GitHub Runner workflows, replace Claude usage with the Diligent binary as the execution engine.
In TUI, make the plan UI float fixed at the bottom of the viewport.

In the web client, clicking + New conversation should enter a draft state instead of eagerly creating a thread: keep URL at '/', keep sidebar list unchanged, and create/hydrate the actual thread only when the first user message is sent.
User prefers framing implementation scope as 'focused on the current task' rather than 'minimal changes'/'최소 수정'.
User wants stale or no-longer-valid knowledge entries to be actively updated or deleted rather than left in place.

Do not store immediately planned implementation intent as knowledge. Anti-pattern: adding a knowledge entry like 'user wants to build some feature' and then immediately saying 'now I will start implementing it.' Knowledge should capture durable preferences, patterns, corrections, discoveries, or actual backlog items worth preserving across sessions, not transient intent for the current turn.
In TUI, when resuming a conversation, do not print the entire past message history; show a bounded/condensed resume view instead.
In the web client, after the user answers a question/request_user_input prompt, the resulting tool block should be rendered in the conversation UI.

For the passion-junior skill, the user prefers it to autonomously proceed with any work that can be advanced independently from repository context, without waiting for confirmation; the user will evaluate the result through the PR.
By default, exclude collab tools (spawn_agent, wait, send_input, close_agent) from subagents so child agents cannot create or manage further subagents unless explicitly allowed.
Strengthen subagent spawn prompts/instructions to explicitly forbid spawning or coordinating additional subagents unless the parent explicitly requests it.
For userId fallback, generate a random UUID on first run and persist it for reuse across launches instead of deriving identity from MAC address or other hardware identifiers.
Provide a way to disable unnecessary built-in agents.
Implement micro-compaction: prune old tool results to reduce retained history.

Support package/build-time configuration of the hidden Diligent storage namespace so product variants can use a custom base directory (for example `.overdare` instead of `.diligent`) for both project-local and home-level state. For branded desktop builds, add conditional one-time migration only when the target namespace does not exist and the legacy `.diligent` directory does exist. Runtime-only bundle updates still cannot independently switch namespace because the existing shell/launcher owns and resolves the global runtime root before launching the updated runtime.
Investigate and fix occasional garbled characters when pasting text in the TUI.

Provider-native web assistant blocks now stream live through assistant message deltas via content_block_delta. TUI/Web should render provider_tool_use, web_search_result, and web_fetch_result as soon as they arrive, while avoiding duplicate re-render on message_end. For diagnostics, DILIGENT_DEBUG_WEB_TOOLS=1 logs both raw web payload stages ([llm:web-tools]) and emission timing/fallback decisions ([llm:web-tools:emit]) so delayed provider delivery versus completed-response fallback can be distinguished.
User prefers provider-native web blocks to be presented in a UI format similar to ordinary tool calls rather than as a distinct assistant-content style.

Thread resume behavior for tool definitions: if the thread runtime is already in-memory in the current app-server process, resume reuses existing agent/tools (no rebuild). If resumed from persisted state (e.g., after restart or missing in-memory runtime), runtime creation path rebuilds default tools via createRuntimeAgent -> buildDefaultTools.
For the VS Code extension UX, the user prefers the chat surface to live at the same hierarchy level as code editors rather than being confined to the extension sidebar/panel.

For the VS Code extension conversation UI, the user prefers assistant output to render as plain flowing text similar to the TUI rather than boxed block-heavy cards, and wants appropriate collapsible treatment for secondary/detail-heavy sections.

For the VS Code extension, do not introduce a VS Code-specific protocol. It should compose the existing shared protocol and fix current implementation drift before adding higher-level UX enhancements.

User wants the tech-lead skill/workflow to run on a 50-commit cadence from the last reviewed commit and to register actionable follow-up work as GitHub Issues. User also wants the passion-junior skill to work from existing GitHub Issues by self-assigning one issue at a time instead of using tech-lead review documents as its task queue.

OVERDARE product-owned TypeScript bundled tools live under `apps/overdare-ai-agent/sidecar`, not `packages/runtime` or `packages/web`. `apps/overdare-ai-agent` is the single product app root: Rust launcher/update/bootstrap code owns process lifecycle and storage migration, while `sidecar/` owns the TypeScript web-server entrypoint and bundled product tools. The sidecar imports `@diligent/web/server`, creates product providers, and is compiled by `scripts/build-overdare-sidecar.ts` into the OVERDARE `diligent-web-server` binary. `packages/runtime` owns only generic bundled-provider contract/catalog/app-server plumbing; `packages/web` stays generic and accepts injected `bundledToolProviders`.
